#3178. Why Ecovyst Stock Topped the Market Today

The specialty chemicals company had a beat-and-raise third quarter.

Investors considered specialty chemical manufacturer Ecovyst (ECVT +2.11%) to be a special stock on Wednesday. They traded it up after the company published its third-quarter results that morning, and it closed the day more than 2% higher. That trounced the under 0.4% gain of the bellwether S&P 500 index.

For the period, Ecovyst's sales were just under $309 million, which bettered the year-ago quarter by 51%. However, that total includes sales from Calabrian, a business the company acquired at the end of June.

Getty Images. Image source: Getty Images.

In terms of profitability, net income not under generally accepted accounting principles (non-GAAP, or adjusted) increased by 18% to over $25 million, or $0.23 per share.

With those results, Ecovyst notched a pair of beats on the consensus analyst estimates. The more convincing one was revenue, as those pundits collectively modeled for under $282 million. Their adjusted earnings per share (EPS) estimate was $0.21, meanwhile.

In its earnings release, Ecovyst attributed its organic growth largely to increased export demand, which boosted sales of both regenerated and virgin sulfuric acid.

As for the proximate future, Ecovyst quoted CEO Kurt Bitting as saying, "Given current refining economics, we anticipate high refinery utilization through year-end, and we expect demand across our portfolio to remain healthy for the rest of the year."

In line with that bullish forecast, the company raised its guidance for full-year adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) to a range of $208 million to $212 million. That's well above both the previous estimate ($195 million to $207 million) and the pre-Calabrian 2025 result of $172 million.

It isn't easy to find a thriving company in the specialty chemicals space these days, and it looks as if Ecovyst has hit the sweet spot with its in-demand products. It also seems to be integrating Calabrian smoothly and quickly. With all that, its rosy forecast is fully believable, making it a stock to watch in its sector.

#3177. I Took the iPhone 18 Pro Max to Japan and Its New Camera System Brought Out My Creative Side

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The iPhone 18 Pro got fun new camera features and they made my bucketlist travel destination more memorable.

Apple gave its pro iPhones a crucial camera and battery boost this year. As a frequent traveler, these upgrades had me stoked for the iPhone 18 Pro Max, so I took it with me to Japan. Going vintage watch hunting through the streets of Tokyo to 6 a.m. hikes in Kyoto’s Fushimi Inari and the Shinto shrines, I used the new phone as my main camera. It made me rethink my shots, pushed me to experiment more with my perspective and surprised me in the most unexpected ways.

The variable aperture, manual camera controls and new Photographic Styles make the iPhone 18 Pro the most fun camera system from Apple, even if they are just minor upgrades from the 16 Pro and 17 Pro. The starburst effect in f4, grain in Photographic Styles and adjustable shutter speeds add drama, depth and more personality to even the most mundane shots.

From my time landing in Osaka to landing back in Delhi, the iPhone 18 Pro Max had me experimenting for two weeks. Here’s what I shot and how the new upgrades made an impact on my first trip to Japan.

The iPhone 18 Pro has manual controls baked into the Camera app. I can adjust the focus, choose the lens aperture from four stops, pick a shutter speed and select the white balance without needing to install a third-party app. The variable aperture is the main attraction here, letting me experiment with lighting as I visited various shrines.

You can go from f/1.48 to f/4 on iPhone 18 Pro’s main camera to adjust the amount of light hitting the sensor. Apple has programmed the f/4 (its narrowest) setting to give you a starburst effect with bright light sources, which showed up as light blobs on older iPhones. I used f/4 to get starbursts from the reflections of sunlight hitting a shrine:

Not every photo needs this effect, but starbursts add a unique style that you won’t find on any other phone. I was busy framing my shots to get the most reflections and the cameras didn’t disappoint.

Combine this with adjustable shutter speeds (takes a bit getting used to) and it leads to endless new possibilities. On the night I landed in Osaka, I went out for a stroll near my hotel, and took about 250 shots at a red light. I only got a few decent light trails, but it forced me to get more creative with my photography

After a few days I finally got the shot of a moving car stabilized with a blurred background. The trick? Finding the right shutter speed (1/15 in this case) through trial and error and moving my iPhone at the same speed as the car. At night, I stuck to 1/2s for moving vehicles with handheld stabilization. I’m happy with the results.

From light trails at night to a speeding car in daylight, the iPhone 18 Pro Max cameras create an effect that was previously only possible through third-party apps. This is different from simply taking a live photo and tapping Long Exposure in edits. You can track a subject to focus and the rest of the movement creates visual effects like the ones in my photos.

Apple’s manual controls are all about getting creative with your frames. You can then personalize these with the new film look and grain in Photographic Styles. These are like simulations that you’d find on the Fujifilm X100 series or Ricoh GR cameras.

For example, I edited this cyclist shot in the Photos app. I used the Dramatic + Film Style because I liked the blue tint in the sky and background, while keeping the skin tone intact. It gave my shot a moody look without editing the colors on my subject, like a regular filter would.

For these two nature shots, I brought all three aspects: adjustable shutter speed, f4 aperture and new Photographic Styles into a single frame. I love the grain, film and glow effects on the iPhone 18 Pro this year. They make the iPhone cameras exciting again.

However, there are a few things I’d like to change about this software.

The grain and film look are nice additions but I’d have loved to adjust the intensity of grain, much like my Vivo X300 Ultra. The current look is good for photos shot in bright light, but anything dim starts looking too artificial. The grain is too aggressive for most situations.

As much as I appreciate the new manual controls, I’m not fond of their placement in the Camera app. I missed a slow shutter shot of the Shinkansen because I was busy finding the manual control. These bullet trains are just too fast!

The new manual controls can be added to the top of the viewfinder or accessed through the six-dot settings menu at the bottom-right corner. In both positions, they aren’t made for one-handed use. It’d also be nice if I could adjust the position of certain toggles in the six-dot menu on the viewfinder. I need the aperture and shutter speed on the rightmost side, but I can’t edit it. The two icons aren’t instantly recognizable up on top. I believe that if I could change their positions in the bottom menu, I’d recognize them faster and remember their positions for a more reliable shooting experience.

Then comes the Camera Control. It doesn’t support any of the new manual controls. So, you can’t adjust the shutter speed or choose an aperture. If I have an extra button dedicated to the camera, I’d ideally like to use it for manual controls. It’d allow faster access to the new features.

In my opinion, Apple should also let us assign two separate Photographic Styles on the front and back cameras. On my trip, I had set a Fuji-like look for street photography, which seemed great for my surroundings but not for my selfies. You can always edit these photos in post, but if I’m out with new friends and sharing these photos with them, it’d be easier if I could set two different Photographic Styles for the front and back cameras.

During my trip, I didn’t have to top up my iPhone 18 Pro Max more than once a day. I left it on charge overnight as my mornings were reserved for breakfast and figuring out the train connectivity through Google Maps. (Seriously, I don’t know how I’d travel without this app.)

Japan is a unique mix of next-gen technology and decades-old systems. While it has a Suica card for public transport, I couldn’t add it to my Apple Wallet. Most stations don’t accept Visa contactless payments. I had to run to the nearest 7/11 to get cash and purchase train tickets. Some markets are also cash-only, so my iPhone was constantly running Maps, Music and Camera for a healthy 6 hours a day.

It lasted me through long photography sessions and constant navigation without any issues. In my experience, this is a huge upgrade over my iPhone 17 Pro Max, which required two charging instances if I was pushing it with Camera and Maps usage. The new model also doesn’t get as warm as its predecessor. I noticed the heat dissipates quicker when using the iPhone 18 Pro Max without a case. I’ve tried three cases so far and each one traps heat, making it warm to touch. If you can, going caseless is a good idea on the new pro iPhones.

The added battery life is a fantastic addition to this year’s model, and will be appreciated by anyone who travels regularly. This is in line with CNET’s tests, where the iPhone 18 Pro Max emerged as the longest-lasting battery life of any iPhone Apple has ever made. I just wish it was lighter. At 248 grams, it is one of the heaviest phones on the market and if you put a case on it, the iPhone 18 Pro Max becomes bulky and hard to use with one hand. I hope Apple finds a way to give us an even better battery life in a lighter form next year.

On the front, you also get a smaller Dynamic Island, which can expand to show up to three live activities (up from two) simultaneously. However, some apps aren’t yet fine-tuned to accommodate the change. On one occasion, when I ordered food through Uber, while running Spotify and Maps navigation, the Live Activity cut the “2” in 27-minute ETA for the order. So I had the next direction, music and an incorrect ETA as glanceable info on top of my screen.

Japan was one of my bucket-list locations and I’m glad I took the iPhone 18 Pro Max with me. This is the most fun I’ve had with an Apple camera system in a long time. From the shrines in Kyoto to the riverside walk along the Sumida River in Tokyo, these cameras invited me to get more experimental. The film-like Photographic Styles, new manual controls and variable aperture helped me get more creative with my perspectives.

It took me more than 250 shots at a crossing in Osaka before I figured out which shutter speed was ideal for what occasion. Similarly, I experimented with my frames to find the best angles for the starburst effect in f/4. Then came the film simulations in Photographic Styles to stylize my shots within the Photos app. All of these new iPhone camera features give me a more analog feel, and I’m here for it.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max, thankfully, has the battery life to support my curiosity and slow learning pace. Through my trips last year, I had to carry a power bank with me, but the iPhone 18 Pro Max changed that. I’m more confident it will last through the day. While none of those camera features would appeal to casual users, the battery life enhancements and improved heat dissipation are tangible upgrades that would benefit everyone.

Also: iPhone Duo hands-on: Some magical touches

“iPhone Duo is constrained as of today … We’re working hard to get this revolutionary new product into the hands of our customers as quickly as possible. But at this time, it’s really hard to predict when supply and demand will be in balance,” Khan told investors.

So, Santa may not be able to deliver the iPhone Duo this year, but Samsung’s foldables may make it onto Christmas lists across the globe instead.

#3173. Motorola’s $1,600 Signature 27 Is Throwing Every Ultra-Level Phone Feature Together

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Motorola's new Signature 27 has one of the fastest wired charging speeds we've seen for a US phone.

After teasing it during Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Summit in September, Motorola’s $1,600 Signature 27 phone will be unveiled on Thursday, and it clearly wants to make a big impression for that high starting price.

Even with the ongoing RAM shortage leading to higher prices for most phones, it would be understandable to think a $1,600 candybar-style phone sounds extravagant. It is. But it’s actually priced competitively against the 512GB model of the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (also now $1,600 following its own fall price increase).

The Signature 27’s biggest feature could be its 200-megapixel periscope telephoto camera, which is capable of a 3x optical zoom and what Motorola calls a 100x Super Zoom Pro. That camera is joined by a 50-megapixel wide camera, a 50-megapixel ultrawide camera and a 50-megapixel front camera. An Event-Based Vision action sensor will also be included to assist with photographing fast-moving subjects.

But particularly eye-opening to me — as someone who’s constantly tracking how quickly phones can recharge — is that the Signature 27 will have 90-watt wired charging. For context, the Galaxy S26 Ultra and the iPhone 18 Pro Max charge at 60-watt speeds, with both phones being among the fastest we’ve tested. The Signature includes a 7,000-mAh silicon carbon battery, which is a newer battery technology that’s able to pack more capacity into less space.

The phone will have a 6.8-inch 1.5K-resolution display that runs at a 120Hz refresh rate, but has an absurdly high 12,000-nit peak brightness. By comparison, many phones we’ve tested lately have included 2,000- and 3,000-nit brightness levels that make it easy to see the screen in sunny environments.

Powering it will be Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor, which Qualcomm says will be particularly helpful for gaming at high-graphics settings, recording video at 8K resolution as well as 4K at 60 frames per second and for on-device AI tasks. The phone’s audio system is created with a partnership with Bang and Olufsen, which we’ll have to hear but should help tune the phone well for music and movies.

The Signature also gets several Android 17 features that debuted on Google’s Pixel 11 series, including Rambler for voice transcription that uses AI to remove “umm”s from the text as well as understanding commands. There will also be a Create My Widget feature for having Gemini create personalized homescreen widgets, and the ability to use American Sign Language for texting. Motorola’s own Qira AI assistant will also be available on the Signature 27, which Motorola says will work across Lenovo devices.

Like the Razr Fold, the Signature 27 will get seven years of software and security updates — which brings Motorola firmly in line with what Google and Samsung provide to their flagship Pixel and Galaxy phones. The Signature will come in two Pantone colors: the dark coal smoke and the green capulet olive. I am interested in feeling both phones because the coal smoke model is described as having a “tactical weave finish” akin to materials used for cars while the olive is said to have a textile-inspired finish that may be closer to the vegan leather backings we’ve seen on the Razr line.

The Signature 27 may be expensive, but I do see where there may be an audience. With the recent retreat of OnePlus from the US phone market, fans of that brand may be looking for a new gamer-friendly phone alternative with both a high-end processor and fast phone charging. The Signature 27 is also arriving after years of growth for Motorola’s Razr line of foldable phones, which itself has included a number of luxury-minded variants such as Razr phones that include Swarovski crystals.

The Signature 27 will release first in the US, going on preorder on Nov. 19 before going on open sale Nov. 26. Both the coal smoke and capulet olive models will come with 512GB of storage and 12GB of memory.

It’s initially being rolled out to a small group of users in the US whose language is set to English. To find out if you have access, check your Netflix navigation bar for the word “Discover” with a red gem icon next to it and a “New” label.

To support AI Discover, Netflix is also adding a new button next to Play and My List that’ll let you tune your recommendations. You can press this button to keep a recommendation or to request that you don’t be recommended a title again.

Most streaming apps already rely quite heavily on machine learning and AI algorithms to offer user recommendations, even if they’re not marketed as AI features. Though most rely on traditional AI algorithms, like Prime Video’s “Recommended for you” tab, they personalize title recommendations based on your viewing history, likes and dislikes, and rental behavior.

Other platforms offer generative AI and features more similar to Netflix’s AI Discover. For example, YouTube features Gemini-powered searches that let you ask complex questions or use open-ended prompts to get results you want.

Some smart TV interfaces — including including Roku, Fire TV, Google TV, and, coming soon, Apple TV — have also adopted generative AI in their operating systems to let you use voice search with more naturally worded requests, and the system generates cross-platform results.

While I am itching to test this feature to see just how accurate it can be, Netflix hasn’t made it widely available yet. The company will gradually grant users access over the coming weeks, so stay tuned.

#3170. It’s Possible You’ve Been Making Coffee All Wrong: 6 Mistakes a Pro Says to Avoid

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Avoid these brewing blunders for coffee that tastes like the stuff baristas make.

I make coffee every morning, almost without fail. I haven’t always used the same method, and because I bounce between processes to test and experiment with coffee makers, beans and, yes, even K-Cups, I’m open to the idea that I might not always get it right.

According to Sarina Prabasi, the founder of Buunni micro-roastery in New York City, I’m in good company.

Prabasi serves on the board of the Specialty Coffee Association and assures me I’m probably making one or two common coffee-brewing mistakes, like everyone else. Coffee is nuanced; it’s easy to fall into habits—often passed down from family, and often bad.

Whether you brew your morning coffee with a pour-over, French press or espresso machine, here are six coffee mistakes to avoid.

Even the slightest film of soap residue can taint your next cup.

Ditching the soap for your coffee pot and pour-over immersion brewer might seem like dubious advice. In reality, your coffee equipment doesn’t need a scrub down every time you use it. Even small amounts of residue from fragrant dish soap detergent will leave you with a sudsy, subpar pot of coffee.

“It really stays in there; it can mess with the flavor, and so, usually, a good rinse with super hot water is enough for black coffee,” Prabasi said. Oils from the beans may build up over time, so fragrance-free dish soap comes in handy for occasional deep cleaning. A simple rinse with hot water will more than suffice for daily use, however. Save yourself time and avoid any unwanted “soap scum” notes that might interrupt the notes of your single-origin Sidama natural roast.

Coffee beans are one pantry staple you shouldn’t buy in bulk.

Buying in bulk can save time and money at the grocery store, but it can disappoint coffee drinkers. Buying smaller quantities of beans helps you avoid stale, flat coffee, especially for average drinkers and households with one or two people. Probasi told us that you’ll know coffee has gone stale because it “can taste like a shadow of itself.”

The roaster recommends checking the coffee label for a roast date within one month, ideally within two weeks. (Keep in mind, the “best buy” date is different and isn’t an indicator of freshness.) If you don’t like grinding at home, the roast date should be on the fresher side.

But you needn’t panic about the declining flavor in your cupboard like a ticking time bomb. “Every day post-roast doesn’t mean it’s losing freshness, but after two weeks, I’d say it starts to go down,” Prabasi said. Store coffee in an airtight container but avoid the humid fridge with its plethora of smells that can stick to the beans.

You can find tutorials online recommending brewers, scales, tampers, water filters, grinders and miscellaneous techniques to make the perfect cup. Experimentation is key to crafting your favorite brew but only if you start with the basics. “So just adjust only the water in the beginning,” Prabasi said.

If you don’t have a kitchen scale, the roaster told us the rule of thumb is to start with two tablespoons of ground coffee per cup of water. The finer the grind, the stronger your coffee will taste, so adjust the grounds-to-water ratio accordingly. If that seems too weak or too strong, then adjust by adding more or less coffee at the same grind level.

Beyond the basics, you can get creative. “If your coffee is too sour, it’s maybe that you prefer a dark roast,” Prabasi said. Coffee too bitter? You can adjust the roast type by buying a level down, such as dark to medium or medium to light. “ If you got a coffee from East Africa, maybe try one from South America, you know, like switch [it] around,” she said. Changing one element at a time ensures you know which step affected the result, for better or worse.

Filling your coffee pot with tap water will yield less-than-ideal flavors. For most of us, filtered water will make a big difference in your coffee’s final flavor. Tap water often contains by-products that a home water filtration system can easily remove.

Almost all tap water in the US is disinfected with low levels of chlorine. This chemical helps keep drinking water safe as it leaves treatment centers but can alter the taste and smell of tap water. Chloramines can also strip lead and copper from pipes, by-products that can affect even the most carefully prepared coffee.

Smell can be a dead giveaway that your coffee has gone stale. Prabasi explains that you should immediately open a bag of beans or ground coffee and smell the roasted coffee scent. Aroma is a key indicator of flavor. No aroma means a serious lack of taste.

Prabasi said stale coffee can taste muddy or flat and lack any complex tasting notes that a bag might list on its label. “ That’s why I think for in the coffee profession, so much of what we do is tasting coffee,” she said. “From the farm to the coffee shop, every step of the way coffee gets tasted or cupped, in our vernacular.”

Old coffee isn’t likely to make you sick, so there’s no need to toss it. You might, however, want to shift from taking your coffee black. Making iced coffee is a simple way to mask the lack of tasting notes. An immersion brewer also lets you steep the grounds longer to add a bit more flavor after the coffee has dulled.

Don’t skimp on organic coffee even if it costs a few bucks more.

The multitude of coffee brands at the grocery store can feel overwhelming. To help sift through the masses, Prabasi explains the organic coffee label is a sign of quality that’s important for coffee.

“If you can, then I think for coffee and tea, organic is really important because coffee and tea crops, especially from large farms, tend to get really over-sprayed,” Prabasi said. Pesticides are sprayed right onto the coffee cherries, and coffee is unlike an apple that you can wash or a banana that you peel before eating. Tea leaves go through a similar process, and anything left on the leaves then steeps into your mug.

The coffeehouse owner made it clear that she doesn’t believe coffee needs to be expensive to be considered “good.” Great coffee comes in a variety of price points. ” I think the care that goes into sourcing it, to roasting it, or just serving it, I would be looking for those things,” Prabasi said. The organic label is a helpful place to start.

For more coffee intel, here’s how to read coffee labels and the best travel mugs of 2026, tested by CNET.

For earning rewards, the Citi Strata Premier® Card is the winner. Although it's not an American Airlines credit card, it can make it easier to accumulate AAdvantage miles on many purchases with its higher earning rates and the option to transfer ThankYou points to American.

Still, the Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® can help you achieve AAdvantage elite status and offers perks when flying American Airlines, including a free checked bag and preferred boarding. The Citi Strata Premier® Card is a better fit for travelers who want to earn American Airlines miles without committing all their rewards to a single airline program.

Although the Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® is an American Airlines credit card, the Citi Strata Premier® Card can be a faster way to accumulate AAdvantage miles on many purchases.

That's because Citi Strata Premier® Card holders can transfer ThankYou points to American Airlines AAdvantage — and several other loyalty programs — at a 1:1 ratio.

Currently, the Citi Strata Premier® Card offers more rewards than the Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® in every bonus category. On Jan. 24, 2027, when the benefits on the Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® change, that will change — but only in a couple of narrowly defined categories: select streaming services and eligible Rides and Rails purchases, which include taxis, rideshares, subways and trains. Unless those categories make up a significant portion of your spending, the Citi Strata Premier® Card will likely yield more points overall, even if your ultimate goal is American Airlines miles.

The Citi Strata Premier® Card also offers a $100 annual hotel benefit when you book a single hotel stay of $500 or more, excluding taxes and fees, through Citi Travel. Using the full benefit can more than offset the card’s annual fee, and hotel bookings through Citi Travel earn 10 ThankYou points per dollar.

Just keep in mind that booking through Citi Travel may mean giving up hotel loyalty program benefits you would receive by booking directly. Whether the $100 hotel perk offers enough value to justify booking through Citi Travel will depend on the property, the rates available and how much you value those hotel loyalty benefits.

One of the biggest advantages of the Citi Strata Premier® Card is the ability to earn ThankYou points, which can be transferred to several airline and hotel loyalty programs. If you want the option to transfer points to American Airlines but also see value in the card’s other airline and hotel partners, the Citi Strata Premier® Card is a better choice.

The Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® comes with several benefits that can significantly offset the annual fee:

Free checked bag: Get a free first checked bag on domestic American Airlines itineraries for the primary cardholder and up to four companions traveling on the same reservation. If you check bags with American, this benefit alone could make the card worth getting.

Preferred boarding: The primary cardholder and up to four companions on the same reservation receive preferred boarding.

American Airlines Vacations discount: Save 10% on eligible American Airlines Vacations packages.

Inflight discount: 25% off inflight food and beverage purchases. This perk is being replaced on Jan. 24, 2027, with an inflight statement credit.

$125 flight discount: Spend at least $20,000 during your card membership year and renew the card to receive a $125 American Airlines flight discount. This perk is also changing in 2027; see below.

Starting Jan. 24, 2027, the card will offer:

Inflight statement credits: Receive up to $100 back in statement credits annually on inflight purchases. This replaces the old 25% off inflight food and drink purchases.

$150 flight discount: Spend at least $20,000 during your card membership year and renew the card to receive a $150 American Airlines flight discount. This replaces the $125 flight discount; the spending requirement is the same.

The inflight statement credits, in particular, will be easy to maximize and could potentially offset a meaningful portion of the card’s annual fee. Combined with the ability to earn Loyalty Points toward elite status and the card’s other perks, that can make the card more valuable for American’s flyers.

The Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® offers Turo credits. You receive up to $180 annually in statement credits on eligible Turo rentals, with up to $30 back per eligible rental.

On Jan. 24, 2027, the card will add several more perks:

It’s unusual to see a Global Entry or TSA PreCheck credit on a card with an annual fee under $200. When that perk kicks in, the card could become a good option for travelers who prioritize AAdvantage miles but also want a credit card that fully reimburses the application fee for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck.

» Learn more: American Airlines credit card benefits guide

Cardholders receive 1 Loyalty Point for every eligible AAdvantage mile earned from purchases. That means everyday spending can move you closer to AAdvantage elite status, in addition to earning miles you can redeem for flights. American’s entry-level elite status requires 40,000 Loyalty Points, so putting significant spending on the card can help you reach that threshold.

#3168. Hudson Pacific (HPP) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Occupancy rose a fifth straight quarter as debt fell and studios held steady.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Hudson Pacific Properties, Inc. (HPP -17.05%) reported a period of active leasing and balance sheet management as it navigated shifting demand in West Coast office and studio markets. Management reported that the company prioritized debt reduction through strategic asset dispositions and the opportunistic repurchase of senior notes while maintaining a focus on high-quality assets in technology-driven submarkets. The company stated that leasing activity was primarily concentrated in the San Francisco Bay Area, supported by the ongoing recovery in the technology and venture capital sectors. Furthermore, management indicated that the studio segment showed signs of stabilization with improved production spending in New York and potential legislative catalysts in California.

Operator: Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining us, and welcome to the Hudson Pacific Properties third quarter 26 earnings call. After today's prepared remarks, we will host a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press *1 to raise your hand. To withdraw your question, press 1 again. I will now hand the conference over to Laura Campbell, executive vice president, investor relations and marketing. Laura, please go ahead.

Laura Campbell: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining us. With me on the call today are Victor J. Coleman, chairman and CEO, Mark T. Lammas, President; Harout Krikor Diramerian, CFO and Arthur X. Suazo, EVP of Leasing. This morning, we filed our earnings release and supplemental on an 8-K with the SEC and both are now available on our website along with an audio webcast of this call for replay. Some of the information we will share today on the call is forward looking in nature. Please reference our earnings release and supplemental for statements regarding forward looking information. As well as the reconciliation of non GAAP financial measures used on this call.

Today, Victor will focus on current industry and market trends. Mark will provide detail on our office leasing and studio operations, and Harout will review our financial results and 2026 outlook. Thereafter, we will be happy to take your questions. Victor?

Victor J. Coleman: Thanks, Laura. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to our third quarter call. This was another quarter of steady progress for Hudson Pacific. We signed 534 thousand square feet of new and renewal office leases and our in service office occupancy grew for the 5th consecutive quarter approaching 86%. Together with improved studio performance, that contributed to growth of 8% in same store cash NOI and a core FFO per share year over year, and we are once again raising our full year outlook. We also continue to execute on our disposition plan and strengthen our balance sheet.

Pro forma for our fourth quarter asset sales and senior notes repurchase total liquidity stands at $840 million with our share of debt reduced by 14% year-over-year. And looking ahead, our leasing pipeline stands at 2.1 million square feet with 1.1 million square feet now in advanced stages nearly twice the level of a year ago. A pipeline of similar size set the stage for a very strong 2026. And its greater maturity today further positions us to extend our earnings growth into 2027. Touching on our markets, I am going to begin with the capital fueling demand. US venture backed companies raised $98.4 billion in the third quarter.

While below the outsized first half totals it was roughly double the quarterly levels of 2023 and 2024. Year to date investment now exceeds $515 billion already more than 60% above full-year 2025. With over 70% of it deployed in our West Coast markets. AI remains the primary driver accounting for 20 US rounds of $1 billion or more in the quarter while software also has captured a record share of venture dollars this year. Several indicators support continued funding. US VC fundraising reached over $100 billion through the third quarter already ahead of all of 2025 and a record acquisition exit values are recycling capital back into the ecosystem.

We are mindful of the recent volatility in tech stocks, which is largely centered on the capital spending of the largest platforms, that is a different part of the AI economy from the 1 driving demand in our markets. We will continue to watch how public market sentiments affect private funding, but so far, we have not seen it in our pipeline or tour activity. On the ground, demand continues to build. AI and tech driven leasing is broadening the office recovery across the West Coast with virtually no new supply coming online.

San Francisco posted its 8th consecutive quarter of positive net absorption adding 1.3 million square feet Citywide vacancy has improved 660 basis points over the past year, and asking rents are up nearly 10%. The South Financial District continues to lead having absorbed more than 2 million square feet so far this year. With large blocks in the South of Market quickly disappearing, we expect tenants to widen their searches into adjacent submarkets which should benefit our assets greatly. Silicon Valley delivered its strongest leasing quarter since 2019. At 4.1 million square feet It also absorbed more than 1 million square feet and active tenant demand rose to 12.4 million square feet with Santa Clara among the leading submarkets.

On the peninsula, net absorption turned positive led by Redwood City, Redwood Shores at more than 40% of the region's total, while neighboring Palo Alto remains 1 of the Bay Area's tightest office markets with rents among the highest in the country. Further north, in Seattle, net absorption reached its highest level since 2021. While Downtown Seattle recorded its first positive quarter in nearly 5 years on the strength of the CBD. Pioneer Square has been positive both for the quarter and the year to date. Los Angeles by contrast remains more mixed. Leasing volume rose nearly 12% year-over-year, but net absorption was modestly negative. West Los Angeles captured roughly 40% of all leases.

In Los Angeles while with Brentwood posting positive absorption this quarter. And in Vancouver, class a vacancy downtown fell for the 5th straight quarter to its lowest level since 2022 with no new downtown supply expected until at least 2032. Conditions are setting up for upward pressure on premium rents. Turning to our studio business, production levels in Los Angeles and New York continue to move in different directions. But as Mark is going to discuss, our prime locations are performing well in both. Third Quarter Los Angeles on location shoot days were 5% lower year-over-year and remained 29% below the 5-year average.

New York, meanwhile, is surging with third quarter production spending up 87% year-over-year to $1.6 billion approaching California's $1.8 billion. Filming permits in New York City were up 27% year-to-date as of September. Looking ahead, see potential catalysts for Los Angeles production At the federal level, legislation introduced this fall would create a 20% to 30% film and TV tax credit that stacks on top of the existing state credits and supporters are pushing to pass this before year end. In a bold move this week, governor Newsom proposed raising the state's annual credit from $750 million to at least $1 billion and for the first time extending eligibility to above the line compensation. Closing the gap with competing states.

This proposal will require legislative action and will likely carry into the next administration, but it is a clear signal of the state's commitment to bringing production back. We are also continuing to sharpen the portfolio through opportunistic asset sales and year to date, we closed nearly $190 million of non-core, FFO-accretive dispositions. That includes $90.5 million from the sales of 2001 Gateway and 75 and 99 Howard in the third quarter. 75.5 million of sales for the Skyport Plaza in the fourth quarter and $23 million of sales of the non core assets from Coyote across both quarters.

The office sales took largely vacant capital intensive assets off the books allowing us to focus on capital leasing at our highest potential properties. Consistent with our capital allocation priorities, we use the majority of the net proceeds to delever, which Harout is going to discuss shortly. As we refine the portfolio, its quality continues to be recognized externally. We were named as a GRESB sector leader for the 6th consecutive year and earned a 5-star rating in the 2026 real estate assessment. We also ranked first among US listed office companies for the 2nd consecutive year and 1st among all listed participants in The Americas.

That recognition reflects the investments we have made to keep our portfolio young, modern, efficient, and resilient, as well as our management team's commitment to quality and discipline. Now with that, I am going to hand it over to Mark to talk through leasing and operational details.

Mark T. Lammas: Thanks, Victor. We signed 74 leases totaling approximately 534 thousand square feet in the third quarter with activity evenly balanced between new leasing and renewals. Tech tenants provided a significant source of demand at 28% of activity roughly 2-thirds of our leasing was in the Bay Area where Palo Alto led all submarkets at over 110 thousand square feet. This included a 65 thousand-square-foot renewal and expansion lease with Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies at Clock Tower Square which addressed 1 of the 2028 expirations over 50 thousand square feet. Our in service occupancy increased 310 basis points sequentially to 85.6%, our 5th consecutive quarter of gains and our lease rate climbed 330 basis points to 86.1%.

Adjusted for asset sales and the temporary removal of Fourth & Traction in our Los Angeles Arts District from our in service portfolio, our occupancy and leased rate increased 80 and 100 basis points, respectively on a like for like basis. Regarding Fourth & Traction, the City of Los Angeles adopted seismic retrofit requirements several years ago that applied to the building, so this is work we needed to do. PayPal's recent expiration gives us a window to complete it and we have several prospective long term tenants with requirements of up to 75 thousand square feet interested in the building. that is precisely why we are moving quickly now so the work gets done before they move in.

We expect to finish the seismic work by Q2, at a rent spread of negative 5.6% on a GAAP basis and negative 0.4% on a cash basis. Driven by new and renewal leasing at our Peninsula and Silicon Valley assets. Third quarter net effective rents increased 30% year-over-year, and on a trailing 12-month basis were up 9%. Tour activity remained strong with 116 tours covering nearly 2 million square feet in the third quarter. Tour count was up 13% year-over-year, and the average requirement of 17 thousand square feet remains well above the roughly 10 thousand square feet typical in 2023 and 2024.

Average requirement sizes grew most on the Peninsula and in Silicon Valley where they roughly doubled this quarter, and in Seattle where they rose almost 50%. Even after signing 2.4 million square feet year to date, up 40% from last year, our pipeline has remained above 2 million square feet for 7 consecutive quarters. Roughly 25% above our long-term average. Almost 60% of the pipeline is new leases supporting continued occupancy gains while the renewal portion has grown to over 800 thousand square feet the highest level we have tracked. And as Victor noted, more than 1 million square feet is in late stage negotiations.

The quality and momentum of our pipeline are as strong as we have seen and we are highly confident in our ability to convert a significant portion of it. Turning to our expirations. We have approximately 50% coverage on both the remaining 144 thousand square feet expiring in 2026 and the 1.1 million square feet expiring in 2027. We define coverage as deals and leases, LOIs, or proposals. For the first half of 27, coverage is over 50% including full coverage on the Salesforce and Twilio space at Rincon Center in San Francisco, where we are in late stage negotiations.

Second half 27 expirations are mostly smaller leases, averaging about 6 thousand square feet, and those tenants typically do not engage until about a quarter before expiration. At Washington 1 thousand consistent with last quarter, we have coverage on approximately 65% of the building with active negotiations across 10 tenants whose requirements range up to 125 thousand square feet, including over 60 thousand square feet of late stage deals. Activity at our move in ready spec suites has increased meaningfully since their June completion and plans and pricing are complete for the next phase of spec suites on the 5th and 6th floors.

Beyond our current pipeline, tour activity has picked up noticeably from tenants with near term occupancy needs most of them new to the market. As has been reported, while Weil, Gotshal & Manges, our tenant at Towers at Shores Center in Redwood Shores is winding down operations. Weil occupied 89 thousand square feet across 2 leases. 38 thousand square feet expired after quarter end and the remaining 51 thousand square feet runs through 2038. While recently completed an estimated $700 per square foot build out leaving pristine space that ranks among the Peninsula's best for professional service firms. With in place rents at market.

Beyond the public announcements, we have not heard from Weil about its plans for the Redwood Shores lease. Given the quality of the space and the demand for both the asset and Redwood Shores more broadly, we are confident we could release it efficiently. In our studio segment, our in service stages were 74.7% leased on a trailing 3-month basis in the third quarter stable compared to the prior quarter. Our Hollywood stages remained well leased at 95% and Sunset Pier 94 continued to ramp with its lease rate up another 370 basis points to 82.2%.

In contrast to the broader Los Angeles market, our prime location stages in production fleet saw higher production activity and spend compared to the same quarter last year, though activity softened from the last quarter. Together with lower operating expenses, both sequentially and year over year, and the continued wind down of noncore Coyote operations, our share of core studio NOI improved to $4.3 million from $2.2 million last quarter and up considerably from negative $2.5 million a year ago. Lastly, in terms of additional avenues for value creation, after quarter end, we secured entitlements to convert approximately 164 thousand square feet of office space at 901 Market in San Francisco into 136 residential units above the existing retail.

As we did at 10.9 thousand Washington, we have created real optionality giving us multiple paths to respond to market demand and maximize value. We are advancing construction drawings and evaluating pricing and we will determine the best path forward in the coming quarters. This remains part of a broader effort as we continue to evaluate residential and mixed use opportunities alongside our office assets in Palo Alto, and across the peninsula. And now Harout will take you through our financial results and outlook.

Harout Krikor Diramerian: Thanks, Mark. In the third quarter, total revenues were $180.9 million compared to $180.6 million in the prior year primarily due to asset dispositions most significantly the sale of Element LA, partially offset by improved office occupancy and increased studio production activity. G&A improved 10% to $12.3 million compared to $13.7 million in the prior year resulting from cost cutting initiatives. We reported net loss of $218.1 million or $3.38 per diluted share compared to $130.5 million or $2.12 per diluted share the prior year. Primarily driven by noncash impairments of Skyport Plaza and Hill 7 and a loss on the sale of 875 And 899 Howard.

Deconsolidation loss related to Sunset Glen Oaks accounted for the loss reported in the prior year period. Excluding these items, our underlying performance continued to strengthen. Core FFO grew to $18.6 million, up approximately 11% from $16.7 million in the prior year and increased approximately 8% on a per diluted share basis to $0.28 from $0.26. This was driven by higher same store NOI across both our office and studio properties and lower non real estate depreciation from the wind down of noncore Coyote operations, partially offset by asset sales. Adjustments to FFO totaled negative $2.8 million or negative $0.04 per diluted share primarily reflecting gains on non core Coyote lease terminations.

A prior period property tax refund, and the sale of nonreal estate assets partially offset by noncore Coyote costs. This compares to positive $2 million or $0.03 per diluted share in the prior year. We grew same-store cash NOI 8.3% to $85.2 million, compared to $78.7 million in the prior year. Driven by improved office occupancy and increased studio production activity. Turning to the balance sheet. We ended the quarter with $956 million of liquidity, including $161 million of unrestricted cash and full availability of $795 million on our revolver. Net debt to undepreciated book value was 32.1%, and our debt was 100% fixed or capped. At a weighted average interest rate of 4.9%.

During the quarter, together with our joint venture partner, we extended the $1.1 billion Hollywood Media portfolio CMBS loan to November 2027. Providing additional flexibility as we continue to execute our business plan for the portfolio. The extension required no principal pay down. The spread is unchanged, and we fixed SOFR at 3.5% through the extended maturity slightly better than the swaps it replaced. Subsequent to the quarter end, we repurchased $200 million of senior notes $100 million each of our 2027 and 2028 notes at a discount to par. We funded the repurchase with cash on hand and borrowings under our revolver.

We then closed sales of Skyport Plaza and a non-core Coyote asset and used the net proceeds to pay down the revolver to $30 million. Pro form a for these transactions, HPP's share of debt is $700 million, a reduction of $425 million or 14% from a year ago, and HPP share of net debt to cash adjusted EBITDAre improves to 11.4x from 11.8x at quarter end. Pro forma liquidity is $840 million consisting of $75 million of unrestricted cash $765 million of revolver availability. Which includes $333 million of commitments expiring this December. Beyond the senior notes, our remaining 27 maturities are nonrecourse, Property level joint venture loans primarily the Hollywood Media portfolio CMBS, which we just extended.

For our 2027 and 2028 maturities, we expect to utilize a combination of liquidity, asset sales, and capital markets in a disciplined manner. Interest expense for the quarter was $40.9 million, which improved modestly from the prior year. $117.4 million year-to-date, a 12% improvement versus the first 3 quarters of 2025. Wrapping up our 2026 outlook, we are increasing and narrowing our full year core FFO to a range of $1.15 to $1.21 per diluted share up from the prior range of $1.12 to $1.20. This updated range reflects at the midpoint approximately 1 cent of outperformance in the third quarter compared to our initial expectations as well as approximately 1 cent attributable to improved expectations for the fourth quarter.

While we have received no indication that Weil Gotshal will stop paying rent, we have taken a conservative approach and excluded their rent from our guidance for the balance of the year. The 200-basis-point improvement to average in service office occupancy reflect actual results for the first 3 quarters and estimates for the fourth quarter. The 175-basis-point improvement to same store property cash NOI growth reflect the full year estimates of the properties which now contribute to the same-store pool. In both cases, the improved estimates are essentially attributable to sales of 875 Howard and Skyport Plaza, and the temporary removal of Fourth & Traction from the in service and same store portfolio. For seismic upgrades ahead of re-leasing.

After these changes, the company would have likely maintained its prior outlook on both metrics. As a reminder, this updated range excludes the previously announced wind down of noncore Coyote operations from core FFO. And as always, our outlook excludes potential dispositions, acquisitions, or capital markets activity, beyond those completed to date. With that, I will turn the call back to Victor for closing remarks.

Victor J. Coleman: Thank you, Harout. This was another quarter of steady execution. Leasing remains strong. Occupancy continues to grow, and we further strengthened our balance sheet. With improving demand supporting the recovery in our markets, a healthy pipeline, and potential tailwinds from proposed federal and state production incentives were well positioned heading into 2027. We look forward to sharing more on our Investor Day on December 1st, where we will provide a deeper look at our long term strategy, the outlook for our office and studio businesses, and our capital allocation priorities heading into 2027. Thank you to the entire Hudson team for their hard work and to our tenants, partners, and shareholders for their continued support.

Operator, with that, let's turn it over for questions.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press 1 to raise your hand. To withdraw your question, press *1 again. We ask that you pick up your handset when asking a question to allow optimum sound quality. If you are muted locally, please remember to unmute your device. Your first question comes from the line of Blaine Heck with Wells Fargo. Blaine, your line is open. Please go ahead.

Blaine Heck: Great. Thanks. Good morning out there. You have made additional progress with the asset sales and subsequent note repurchases. But I was hoping you could walk us through just a general overview of the sources uses for the remainder of upcoming unsecured maturities how much you are expecting can be addressed with available cash and additional asset dispositions? And whether you expect to need to raise debt or equity capital for any significant portion of those maturities?

Victor J. Coleman: So thanks, Blaine. I will start with we are not remotely interested in raising equity at these levels, and we do not need to raise equity to address our debt issues. Our first maturity of the debt comes due at the end of next year, And as you noted, we have already taken care of it, $200 million of the $750 million. So we are down at $550 million. We have got multiple areas that we are evaluating. And, if you come to our investor day, we are going to outline a plan that is going to detail it throughout all of 2028, and we are comfortable on our plan.

To give you some highlights, we do have some additional assets, which we are not talking about now. Very few that are going to fall in the disposition category, and we also have JV opportunities with additional assets that we are going to announce lease up on for fully leased assets and long term maturities with credit tenants. That are unencumbered that we can also convert. So we have lots of optionality, as we said, We are attacking this plan methodically as we have dictated. And to date, we have executed it exactly how we have looked.

Blaine Heck: Okay. Great. Thanks, Victor. And you executed on the CMBS extension this quarter. So I was hoping you could provide a little commentary on any further discussions you have had with Netflix and whether you have gained any insight on how they are thinking about their futures space needs between your properties and potentially Sanford.

Victor J. Coleman: Yeah. I cannot comment on San Francisco other than the fact that Netflix has not closed that transaction. And, they are not deciding to close it until, sometime maybe later in the year. Or not. that is not a concern of ours. I can tell you that the replacement of San Francisco for their existing office does not fit the footprint as we have talked about in the past. We have and continue to have very fruitful, very productive conversations with them. I think we will have some resolution on some levels of that hopefully, by year end. And continuing these conversations, positively for them to extend beyond 2031 is looking in the direction that we are comfortable with.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Jana Galan with Bank of America. Jana, your line is open. Please go ahead.

Jana Galan: Thank you. Good morning, and congrats on the quarter. I appreciated all the leasing commentary and being that it was about 2-thirds in the Bay Area. I am curious for the forward $1.1 million pipeline, if you could comment on geographic distribution and maybe mix of new and renewal within that?

Arthur X. Suazo: Sure. This is Arthur. You know, so the mix of new and renewal is in the. Within the pipeline is also 60-40, 60% new Growth tenants. And relative to the distribution of the pipeline, again, 2-thirds of the pipeline is in the Bay Area, The quickest growing portion of our pipeline and tour activity for the last 2 quarters has been Seattle. And so the next large movers will be in Seattle and I believe will continue to be in Seattle. And, of course, Seattle, Vancouver, and LA make up a small portion of that pipeline.

Jana Galan: And anything new on Washington 1 thousand or anything you can share on kind of the activity of the larger space?

Arthur X. Suazo: Yeah. Absolutely. So, you know, we continued the momentum that we had, you know, last quarter. Currently, there are 10 deals in negotiation, 3 of which are on the 3 remaining, market ready suites. 1 of those deals is in late stages. for 15 thousand square feet. The remaining 7 deals in negotiation, 1, 50 thousand square feet is in late stage late stage leases. And the restaurant is in various phases behind that Behind that, you know, we have 6 tenants who are looking for more market ready suites that have really started to tour and be in discussions with us.

So we have planned and we have priced the next phase call it 2 floors of market ready suites that we are going to be ready to go once we are in leases with, the others. Thank you.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Tom Catherwood with BTIG. Tom, your line is open. Please go ahead.

William Catherwood: Thank you, and good morning, everybody. Mark, maybe in your prepared remarks, you mentioned strength in Redwood Shores. Multiple times, that is been 1 of the markets that has sort of lagged behind the recovery of your other Peninsula assets. Can you talk a little bit about what is changed there in terms of demand? And then maybe how much progress do you think you can make there in the near term?

Mark T. Lammas: Yes. We are well leased. Generally speaking, in Redwood Shores. I do not know that a lot has changed. I mean, we have seen steady demand from smaller tenants throughout that market and well diversified, you know, professional services, tech, obviously, given its location. And so I think we have just benefited from what has been core, steady quarter over quarter demand. We have captured. We have outpaced the overall market consistently I, you know, I do not know what else to say about it. I mean, I. Arthur can add some further color on it, though.

Arthur X. Suazo: Yeah. Absolutely, Tom. You know? So I think the strength of that market for us is a small tenant in our market-ready, move in ready suites, You know, we have deployed probably over 200 thousand square feet over the last several years. Right now, we have well over I would say, close to 100 thousand square feet of move-in ready suites. With great coverage, and that is how we are outperforming the market. We understand the size of the tenant is, as Mark indicated. They are generally under 20 thousand square feet. And that is precisely how we are meeting the market.

William Catherwood: Let me just follow-up on that. I get the, you know, things are getting better. But if we go back to a year ago, I mean, you know, yes, you have added 500 basis points of leasing there, but you have added a lot more in other parts of the peninsula. So is this something that you think you can get into the mid 80s as we move forward? Historically, it has tended to lag behind. How much how deep is that potential demand that you are looking at?

Arthur X. Suazo: Yeah. I mean, we were we were well into the eighties. I feel like we can get back well over 80 as well. there is been lift, as you know, on the Peninsula there is been significant lift with Palo Alto. With Redwood City, and we are now seeing this wave of you know, small to midsized tenants you know, that we are, you know, aggressively pursuing. So yeah, we could get well into the eighties. Okay.

William Catherwood: And then just last 1 for me. Maybe moving over to Quixote, With the $23 million sale, what is left, and then kind of what is the timeline for resolving the remainder of non core? And I get it could be lumpy. But in general, what are your expectations for resolving what is left there?

Mark T. Lammas: In terms of just the wind down, we are down to just a few more leases associated with the noncore Coyote business, and we think those will be wrapped up by year end. I think, you know, just in terms of a scorecard, we are on schedule, if not a bit ahead, and we have been able to. Actually, ourselves at a at a price, if you will, below what we had initially targeted. So we think we are executing extremely well on the wind down. Once it is that wind down is complete, we will be. At that point, will be a transportation company exclusively based in New York and largely in LA.

Roughly 1 thousand vehicles of various types. With 6 or so locations. To either house those vehicles or maintain those vehicles. And importantly, and you see it in our third quarter results, even with show counts sort of stubbornly for now, at least stuck at 70, We almost hit the breakeven target. We were at the negative $600 thousand for the quarter, which is darn close to where we hope to get. And with a. Just a touch of improvement in show count, we think we are we would be at breakeven. So that is kind of where the business we think looks like when the wind down process is over and we will.

And once that is done, we will have to just step back and, you know, kind of assess what comes next.

Victor J. Coleman: Yeah. And just lastly on that piece, Tom. You know, we are still maintaining our market share, which is extremely high for that business. Got it.

William Catherwood: Appreciate the answers. Thanks, everyone.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Ronald Kamdem with Morgan Stanley. Ronald, your line is open. Please go ahead.

Ronald Kamdem: Great. Just starting on the same store NOI. Just in the quarter that you sort of posted. You are thinking about sort of flipping the calendar, what are some of the puts and takes to how same store NOI should evolve with sort of occupancy and commencements and everything. Just trying to get a sense if this level is sort of the right run rate going forward.

Harout Krikor Diramerian: Hey Ronald, great question. So I do not know if we are ready to talk about 2027, but I will give you some high level amounts. But you know, as leasing continues to improve and as free rent burns off, we expect the same store cash NOI to continue to improve. So that is the trajectory. There may be some, you know, additional free rent for new leases in the upcoming year. But, ultimately, the trajectory should be growing. on a go-forward basis.

Ronald Kamdem: Great. And then my second 1 is just the leverage. It looked like it ticked up a little bit during this quarter. Maybe can you talk about just as you are thinking about whether it is funding some of the CapEx for the leases or asset sales and so forth. Just where do you think that should trend to as NOI comes online and you are managing sources and uses? Thanks.

Harout Krikor Diramerian: Sure. So the leverage increased quarter over quarter, but again, below our expectations, and it is almost entirely due to the PayPal lease expiring at Fourth & Traction. So all within our expectations, in fact, we beat our expectations. And I think we said in our prepared remarks when you pro forma in the note repurchase and asset sales, leverage ticked back down. it is going to be a little up and down in the short term, but overall, we expect it to start dropping. And that is our plan. So, again, similar to the same store cash NOI, as free rent burns off, those leverage metrics will definitely increase. and be helpful. that is it for me. Thank you.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of John Kim with BMO Capital Markets. John, your line is open. Please go ahead.

John Kim: Thank you. You talked about 50% coverage on next year's expiration. Was wondering if you could provide some more, commentary on what that comprises of. #3167. Safari finally gets 3 popular browser features – and I can’t wait to try them

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

New developer beta release notes point to deeper Siri AI integration and more Safari customization.

Developer betas for MacOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and iOS 27.3 are here, with a few major upgrades to the Safari browser. Vertical tabs, adaptive dark mode, and deeper Siri AI integration are on the way to the public, but are first in beta for testing.

Also: Your Apple Watch has 2 new controversial listening features – but you have to opt in

Siri AI is expected to be further woven into Music, Messages, Photos, Calendar, and Safari. Adaptive dark mode will allow for any website to be viewed in dark mode, even if the site doesn’t support it. Finally, vertical tabs are pretty straightforward, enabling vertical navigation and drag-and-drop tab reorganization.

Here’s what you can expect when the software goes public in mid-December.

Also: 3 handy iPhone features that make my life easier – even doing laundry

Siri AI gains more access to your Apple devices, allowing more cross-app functionality and the ability to execute complex, multi-step tasks within your apps.

According to 9to5Mac, you can ask Siri AI to create a playlist in Music and save it to your library, request messages to be scheduled for a later send, organize and label photos, and create a detailed calendar invite — all with your voice.

The same reporting also states that Siri AI features will appear in Maps, Weather, Shortcuts, and Notes, signaling that an AI-supercharged Siri will live in every crevice of your Apple devices.

Also: iOS 27 will organize your open Safari tabs now

I’m not one to complete tasks like the ones mentioned above on my iPhone — I’m far more likely to do them on my MacBook Air, since I associate the laptop with productivity. Every blue moon I’ll rearrange my entire Apple Music catalog, every month I fill out my calendar, and sometimes I’ll go through Photos and try to organize it. I can see myself automating certain steps in these tasks, and I’m excited to try it.

A WebKit blog post details that adaptive dark mode is coming to Safari, how it will work, and what users can expect. According to the post, 40% of web page loads are from dark mode users, but only 10% of web pages natively support it.

I’m particularly excited about this feature, as I set my Apple devices to automatically enable dark mode at 7 p.m. to encourage a more relaxing evening scrolling vibe, especially while reading. I read a lot on my MacBook, and in a dark room, a bright page can feel too bright, but dimming my laptop’s display doesn’t quite do the trick.

Also: Your AirPods got better in iOS 27 – three new ways I’m using them

The WebKit blog post states that adaptive dark mode uses “a color matrix to invert the luminosity of colors while preserving hue” and distinguishes between when a page’s color is purely decorative and when it carries substantial meaning, to ensure the user experience remains consistent between light and dark modes.

Vertical browser tabs aren’t a new concept, but they’ll soon be new to Safari. I see the value in vertical tabs: a list view is easier to scan, web page titles aren’t smushed when several tabs are open, and they’re particularly useful when you’re working on a widescreen monitor.

Many people who spend hours using their Mac or MacBook may find this upcoming feature useful. I do believe that Safari is the superior browser for personal use, given its integration with your Apple devices, especially with features like Handoff.

Also: 7 AI-free iOS 27 features that make old iPhones exciting again

However, I do have one major gripe with vertical tabs: they’re usually locked to the left panel, and I prefer the right. If Safari allows this customization, I’ll seriously consider switching from horizontal tabs.

#3165. The Clock Is Running on Apple’s Siri Settlement. How to File Before Dec. 21

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Anyone in the US who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or iPhone 16 model between June 2024 and March 2025 is eligible to file a claim.

Dec. 21 is the last day to file a claim in Apple’s $250 million settlement over delayed Siri features, and payouts could reach $95 per eligible iPhone.

The class covers anyone in the US who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or any iPhone 16 model between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, the stretch when Apple was promoting a more personal Siri that hadn’t arrived yet. Filing takes a few minutes online, and each qualifying phone gets its own claim.

The iPhone 16 went on sale in September 2024 with Apple Intelligence at the center of its marketing. However, the first AI features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, several weeks later, and the most heavily promoted one, a Siri that could pull personal context from your apps, was further delayed in March 2025.

Now you can turn that initial dismay into a payment in Apple’s $250 million legal settlement by signing up at a live website. The opt-in form is available only for a limited time, so get your name in the pool before it closes. Eligible buyers have until Dec. 21 to file, and each qualifying iPhone gets its own claim.

Apple settled a false advertising lawsuit brought by Clarkson Law Firm in May, agreeing to pay $250 million to customers who bought some iPhone models during a specified period. The lawsuit alleged that Apple misled customers by promising AI features that didn’t ship with the new devices. Apple denies all of the lawsuit’s allegations and denies that it did anything unlawful or improper.

If you purchased an iPhone 16 or iPhone 15 at launch, you may be entitled to receive a portion of the quarter-billion-dollar settlement. Payouts between $25 and $95 per eligible device are expected.

“Apple has reached a settlement to resolve claims related to the availability of two additional features. We resolved this matter to stay focused on doing what we do best, delivering the most innovative products and services to our users,” an Apple spokesperson said in an earlier statement to CNET.

The court granted preliminary approval of the settlement on July 17. Then an Aug. 13 order moved up the final approval date by seven months.

“False advertising settlements aim to raise the floor of truth-telling, protect fair competition and increase consumer choice,” said Ryan Clarkson, co-lead counsel on the case and founder and managing partner of Clarkson Law Firm, in a statement to CNET. He claimed it’s the largest false-advertising settlement in history.

Apple lit up its flagship New York City store to resemble Siri’s new color scheme.

As of Sept. 21, you can go to SmartphoneAISettlement.com and enter your information to confirm your eligibility for monetary relief. People whom Apple and the settlement administrator determined would be eligible will also receive email or postal notices from the company Verita directing them to the website.

The claims window closes on Dec. 21, 2026, so you have three months to act.

If you bought one of the following devices between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, you could be eligible to receive a settlement payment:

The iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max are included because they have the processor and memory to run Apple Intelligence features.

It’s estimated that approximately 36 million customers are eligible for this settlement.

When Apple advertised its new iPhone 16 lineup in 2024, it emphasized how the models were optimized for AI features such as an enhanced Siri that could act as an intelligent agent. When the phones did arrive, Apple Intelligence wasn’t yet ready; its first features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, five weeks later.

According to the proposed settlement, “Apple allegedly saturated the market with deceptive ads, inducing consumers to purchase iPhones based on the promise of certain enhanced Siri features.”

Some features of Apple Intelligence did ship soon after the introduction of the iPhone 16 and iOS 18, including Visual Intelligence, Live Translation, Writing Tools, Genmoji and Clean Up. But those weren’t the advanced features Apple highlighted. In fact, the type of intelligent interactions Apple advertised is only starting to show up in Siri AI, which is part of iOS 27, which was released in early September.

According to the settlement, Apple needed to provide the information about affected customers within five days of the settlement approval. As of late July, preliminary approval has been granted by the court.

After the data is provided and verified, a 45-day notice period begins to inform potential consumers that they’re eligible for a payment.

On Aug. 13, US District Court Judge Noël Wise granted approval to push forward the date from Sept. 29, 2027, to Feb. 24, 2027.

Provided approval is granted, the first checks or deposits will arrive sometime within a 60-day window after February next year, depending on court dates and possible extensions.

#3164. Want an AI job? Deployment engineers are earning executive-level pay – up to $1.45M a year

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

AI has ushered in new jobs, and some of them are paying handsomely, according to a new study.

AI engineers are making well over six figures in salary — and plenty more in bonuses and equity, according to data from a new report by executive search firm Christian & Timbers.

Enterprises now pay “elite” AI deployment engineers between $586,000 and $1.45 million annually in total compensation, with senior leaders in the field earning up to $2.25 million, according to the report. This figure approaches the median compensation of executive officers of public companies, the authors note.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ new top stressor

Christian & Timbers is an AI executive search and leadership advisory firm, recruiting CEOs, board members, technology executives, and AI engineers for enterprises. The new report draws on more than 550 interviews with engineers, deployment leaders, and executives conducted from January through June 2026, along with closed and current open offers. The compensation bands are Christian & Timbers’ estimates and represent ranges rather than statistical averages.

“Enterprise CEOs are under pressure to deliver returns for their AI investments. The most important decision is how to build the team that delivers on that goal,” said Jeff Christian, founder and CEO of Christian & Timbers, in a press release.

Also: What workers are really using AI for in 2026 – and what they aren’t

The report noted that the staggering salary range includes base salary, bonus, and annualized equity. Christian & Timbers said it defines an “elite” forward deployment engineer (FDE) as “a senior AI-native deployment builder, typically with 7 to 15 years of experience, including at least two years building and deploying agentic automated workflows that deliver measurable ROI with a documented enterprise impact of $10M or more,” who has also led a team of other forward deployment engineers.

Also: 50% of companies generate value from AI now – here’s how

The large salary ranges reflect increasing enterprise investments in AI talent and employee development. Microsoft, AWS, and OpenAI have announced more than $7.5 billion in corporate and partner investment in AI deployment over the past six months, Christian & Timbers noted in the release.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill

There’s an increasing need to fill roles such as Senior Principal AI Engineer, AI Solutions Engineer, and Head of Deployment — but there is a limited pool of qualified candidates. The firm estimates that only 2,000 of the most senior deployment leaders exist in the US market, according to a previous Christian & Timbers study, which does not meet demand — so companies are competing for the same small group of professionals, hence the increasing salaries.

While the report underscores lucrative yields for certain engineering roles, the firm said that public job titles make comparisons more challenging.

“Christian & Timbers’ elite category spans several titles, while advertised FDE roles cover a broader range of experience and responsibilities. Experienced deployment engineers may be recruited directly or promoted into the work under titles such as staff software engineer or principal AI engineer,” the study said.

Plus, equity and bonus make up 52% to 66% of senior engineer pay, and most job postings don’t include that value in the salary, the report noted.
